theory.overview: Code generation transforms intermediate representations into executable machine code. This involves selecting appropriate instructions, allocating registers, managing the call stack, and generating efficient code for the target architecture.

sections.title: Instruction Selection
sections.content: Mapping IR operations to machine instructions. Complex IR patterns may match multiple machine instructions (instruction combining), while simple patterns map directly.

examples.explanation: Maps to: ADD r1, r2, r3 on x86

sections.title: Register Allocation
sections.content: Assigning IR variables to CPU registers. Since registers are scarce, the compiler must spill variables to memory when necessary using algorithms like graph coloring or linear scan.

sections.title: Calling Conventions
sections.content: Standardized rules for function calls: where arguments go (stack or registers), who saves which registers, how return values are passed, and stack frame layout.

keyConcepts.name: Register Spilling
keyConcepts.description: Moving variables from registers to memory

steps.title: From IR to Assembly
steps.content: Map IR operations to target instructions. Consider instruction costs and addressing modes. Handle operations not directly supported by the target.

steps.title: Live Variable Analysis
steps.content: Compute which variables are 'live' at each point. Two variables interfere if they're both live at any point and cannot share a register.

steps.title: Graph Coloring
steps.content: Build interference graph, attempt to color with N colors (registers). If impossible, spill a variable to stack and retry.

practiceProblems.title: Instruction Selection
practiceProblems.description: Translate: t1 = a + b; t2 = t1 + c (target has 2-operand ADD)
practiceProblems.solution: mov r0, a; add r0, b; add r0, c; // r0 holds result

practiceProblems.title: Register Pressure
practiceProblems.description: Given 3 registers and 5 live variables at same point, what's the solution?
practiceProblems.solution: Spill 2 variables to stack (memory), keep 3 in registers. Reload when needed.

minigame.title: Instruction Selector
minigame.description: Match IR patterns to optimal machine instructions
